author: terencechain
content: but I  don’t think the gloas edge case is an  argument against the eip right. Calling an epoch finalized today is already misleading because the checkpoint only points to its first slot. This EIP moves that boundary in the right direction and in gloas, the finalized execution block would usually move from slot 31 to slot 30, but I don’t think that breaks anything. Contracts can’t read the finalized tag, and I’m not aware of anyone proving this exact relationship on chain. Off chain callers is likely already using the wrong value to begin with. Treating slot 0 of epoch N but N is not finalized
